name: Integrated Circuit

claims.claim_text: What electronic design work consists of has shifted with integration. Early solid-state design meant building transistor circuits out of transistors; the modern equivalent is systems engineering, taking integrated circuits and assembling systems from them, with the functionality of each part sealed inside a box.
claims.quote_verbatim: Everything is in a box called an IC
claims.speaker: Henry Ott
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Henry Ott - Forced FCC Filtering

claims.claim_text: The distinction drawn by practitioners is between integrated circuit design and system-level design: the latter means board level and integrating the result into a whole system, which is what the majority of electronics engineers actually do.
claims.quote_verbatim: taking ICs and stuff and making systems out of them
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: Integration is usually cheaper than assembling the equivalent from separate packages, because the cost consolidates onto the silicon: three packages meeting the same specification typically cost more than one integrated device. The consequence is that designs become less interesting to look at while becoming cheaper to build.
claims.quote_verbatim: the cost is, is consolidated onto the silicon and it makes for boring or boring or designs
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Consolidate All The Things - Zonked Zelotic Zaitech

claims.claim_text: Highly integrated parts are built for a specific problem rather than for generality, and within that problem a discrete implementation rarely competes. The corollary is that outside the intended application the same integration may deliver neither the accuracy nor the capability wanted.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you see this very high-level integration, it's for a very specific problem
claims.speaker: Art Kay
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Art Kay

claims.claim_text: Complex-sounding analog parts decompose into familiar blocks: an instrumentation or difference amplifier is three operational amplifiers with precision resistors, so what the vendor is selling is a packaged system built from the same components a designer would otherwise assemble.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's just three op amps
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Analog Components, First Person Flying and Idea Ownership

claims.claim_text: Functions once built from discrete assemblies migrate into packages as the enabling component shrinks: isolation was implemented with a transformer and separate driver and receiver circuits, and the contribution that made an integrated isolator possible was making the transformers small enough to fit several channels inside an ordinary package.
claims.quote_verbatim: coming up with transformers that were so small, they could be multiple channels could be put into a normal size IC
claims.speaker: Hank Zumbahlen
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Hank Zumbahlen - Zoppa Zumbahlen Zateticism

claims.claim_text: Boards carrying a hundred separate logic devices no longer exist in new design work: the functionality now sits in a microcontroller, in programmable logic, or in a purpose-built device bought from a major manufacturer, and the design activity has moved up to the system level accordingly.
claims.quote_verbatim: Name a modern design that's got, you know, 100 chips on a board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wow, Dave REALLY likes Top Gun

claims.claim_text: Design knowledge accumulates into silicon and the firmware around it, which is what converts a specialist capability into a commodity: an inertial measurement unit that cost hundreds of dollars became a part costing cents, and the engineering that used to be required to build one is now bought rather than performed.
claims.quote_verbatim: you pull all that, that know-how into the silicon design and then maybe the firmware around it
claims.speaker: Dave Young
claims.episode_title: Rebuilding Projects with Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Because the device has already been debugged by its designer, the board-level task reduces to a small set of checks: whether a signal is present and whether the supply is working, with everything beyond that being software. That is what conventional systems electronics engineering has become.
claims.quote_verbatim: the chip's already debugged. Somebody at the higher level's taken care of that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: Engineers report a reluctance to use highly integrated parts, feeling they should be building the function from discrete components instead. The counter-argument is that using what is available is engineering rather than a compromise, and that modern systems could not be built at all without such devices, which is why the catalogues hold hundreds of thousands of parts.
claims.quote_verbatim: No one would be able to do advanced modern systems and designs without using these devices
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Yonderly Yodeling Yobbos

claims.claim_text: The judgment runs the other way as often as not: a fifty-cent integrated circuit should not be specified where a two-cent transistor performs the function.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm not going to put in a 50-cent IC when a 2-cent transistor can do the job
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: Optimisation means different things to different designers, and the answers conflict: to an analog designer it may mean replacing one integrated part with ten or twenty discrete transistors, while measured on total overhead a vendor's complete solution costing a dollar more may be the genuinely optimised choice. Which reading applies depends on whether board area, unit cost or engineering time is the binding constraint.
claims.quote_verbatim: the optimizing can mean different things to different people
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Critical Mass

claims.claim_text: Part selection should be revisited against the actual requirement rather than the assumed one, since a device chosen for higher performance may be delivering capability the design does not need, and the same function may be available in a cheaper part.
claims.quote_verbatim: So do I actually need that higher performance?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Consolidate All The Things - Zonked Zelotic Zaitech

claims.claim_text: Small single-function parts have to be extremely cheap by their nature, because in a design review an additional device cannot be justified on any other basis. Such jelly-bean parts run around twenty-four cents at a thousand pieces and a small number of cents at high volume, and the manufacturer will only engage with a customer at quantities in the hundred thousands.
claims.quote_verbatim: These little parts, by their very nature, have to be extremely low cost
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Senseless Saccadic Shemozzle

claims.claim_text: The choice between a module and the bare devices is a volume calculation: a module gives short time to market and easier development, while implementing the chips directly is cheaper once the deployment is large.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want to have a short time to market, you of course choose the module
claims.speaker: Richard Ginus
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Richard Ginus

claims.claim_text: Component shortage inverted normal purchasing practice: critical integrated circuits were bought years before the designs that would use them existed, which is a poor use of capital and was nonetheless the only way to guarantee the parts would be there.
claims.quote_verbatim: buying parts for things that haven't been designed yet
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner
claims.episode_title: Reunion Impedance Matching and 2023 Predictions

claims.claim_text: On a hundred-part board of which roughly a fifth are active devices, a shortage can make almost every integrated circuit and transistor unobtainable at once. The decision then is between redesigning around what is available, which may take longer than the shortage lasts, and buying through the grey market at whatever price is asked, which customers do when the alternative is not shipping.
claims.quote_verbatim: almost all the ICs and almost all of the FETs you couldn't get
claims.speaker: Dave Young
claims.episode_title: Rebuilding Projects with Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Every forced substitution carries a design cost beyond the part price: the board must be reworked, sometimes repeatedly, and each change reduces confidence in the result, which has to be bought back with additional testing or accepted as risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: having to change ICs every single time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Longevity assurances from a semiconductor supplier are only as durable as the corporate structure behind them: a letter promising ten years of availability is worth nothing if the company is subsequently broken into separate businesses, which makes supplier stability part of the part-selection decision.
claims.quote_verbatim: that stuff is totally valid until your company breaks in half
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Open Source RC & Modelsource - Facinorous Financial Foulness

claims.claim_text: A supplier can fail on logistics rather than on engineering. One manufacturer released so many new devices, on the order of hundreds a year, that customers could not keep track, and then could not deliver them; the available capacity went to the highest-volume customers, leaving smaller designers who had specified the parts unable to obtain them.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were serving, like, really high-volume clients
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: BASIC, Chip companies & Robots - Pernicious Projects, Puppies in Peril

claims.claim_text: Part selection is decided by non-technical factors more often than datasheets suggest: reuse of a device already qualified across a company's products, an engineer's preference for parts they find easy to work with, and refusal to specify a supplier who has caused problems before.
claims.quote_verbatim: we use this on all our products. So we're going to use this again
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Here for a reason

claims.claim_text: Adopting a device late in its life is a deliberate strategy rather than a failure of ambition: a protocol stack at version seven has absorbed years of other people's difficulties, which is what allows one engineer to implement alone what previously required a team, and a new design can leapfrog by starting on the mature part.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm benefiting from all of the. Heartache that happened
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Thermions Aren't A Thing

claims.claim_text: The working assumption during debugging is that the device is behaving correctly, and it is discounted last. That assumption is right most of the time and not always: a fault initially attributed to capacitors and then to the supply converter turned out to be a failed chip presenting as two ohms across the power rail.
claims.quote_verbatim: I usually try and ignore the concept that the chip is wrong until the very end
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Cultural Differences

claims.claim_text: Silicon defects are universal across manufacturers rather than characteristic of any one of them, so choosing a vendor to avoid them is futile. Even a modest eight-bit device contains an enormous number of transistors and circuits, and its maker has already moved on to the next design.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no point trying to avoid it. It's going to happen
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Shine A Light

claims.claim_text: Back-powering happens when a signal is driven into an integrated circuit whose supply is off: the current passes through the protection diodes present on every input and output and partially energises the internal supply rail, so a device that should be unpowered is partly alive and behaves unpredictably.
claims.quote_verbatim: the chip has protection diodes on every IO
claims.episode_title: Measuring Current with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: The applications engineering role at a semiconductor company spans the whole life of a part: helping define its features and pin-out, writing the data sheet, supporting customers and field engineers through early design-ins, validating and debugging the silicon, and releasing it to production before starting the next one.
claims.quote_verbatim: I do everything from helping define new parts, like what features they're going to have, the pin out
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: Manufacturer support quality is regional in a way that affects where hardware development happens. In some regions a problem with a device that cannot be resolved from the data sheet, such as whether a pin has an internal pull-up, is answered by a local representative within a day or two; that level of response is not available everywhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: no issue that within one or two days cannot be solved by bringing in like a local manufacturer's representative
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Merry Keyzermas!

claims.claim_text: Simulating a design imported from schematic capture stalls on the active devices: passive components map onto generic models automatically, while each integrated circuit must exist in the simulator's library or have a model chosen by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: but your chips, well, you know, it's got to be in the library
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Contextual Electronics, ClubJameco and Solderpaste - Lifelong Learning Likelihood

claims.claim_text: A schematic must name the device, not merely carry a reference designator, since forcing anyone reading it to cross-reference a bill of materials to discover what a part is defeats the purpose of the drawing.
claims.quote_verbatim: Put the damn number on the schematic
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Otiose Ontocyclic Opiniasters

claims.claim_text: Protection against transients is applied in two places rather than one: where cables enter the product, and again at the sensitive devices themselves, on the reasoning that the entry protection will not catch everything.
claims.quote_verbatim: Where the cables enter, I try and protect that. And then I go and try and protect the sensitive IC devices
claims.speaker: Henry Ott
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Henry Ott - Forced FCC Filtering

claims.claim_text: Thermal behaviour is instrumented by placing small resistance temperature sensors directly onto the packages of interest, which resolves heat sources and sinks and the thermal path through the assembly rather than giving a single board temperature.
claims.quote_verbatim: small RTDs that you can place right on ICs on your board
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Chris Osterwood

claims.claim_text: Making a usable integrated circuit outside an industrial setting is separated from making a single device by many orders of magnitude of complexity. Producing one transistor or one light-emitting diode is achievable; producing something with logic levels, packaging, leads and pins that can be designed into a circuit is the actual problem, and the market's abundance of cheap qualified parts removes most reasons to try.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's easy to do one LED or one transistor, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ben Krasnow - Sprauncy Saccadic Spintherism

claims.claim_text: What actually lowers the barrier to custom silicon is documentation and access rather than equipment. A process development kit is the fundamental information needed to create an integrated circuit on a given process, and an open one combined with shared fabrication runs is what allows designs to be made without a foundry relationship.
claims.quote_verbatim: PDK stands for Process Development Kit
claims.episode_title: Building wafer.space with Tim Ansell

claims.claim_text: An open silicon programme can permit commercial use provided the design itself is open, on the reasoning that a healthy ecosystem needs companies contributing to it and building the unglamorous parts, in the same way that commercial contributors sustain widely used open-source software.
claims.quote_verbatim: As long as your design is open source, there's no other conditions at the moment
claims.speaker: Tim Ansell
claims.episode_title: Discussing the Open Source PDK with Tim Ansell

claims.claim_text: Pin count constrains how much of a system fits on one die, which in turn dictates the architecture: a fixed number of channels per package forces a split into a control device and separate function devices, and two teams working independently on the same problem arrived at near-identical partitioning because the constraints funnel the choices.
claims.quote_verbatim: it sort of goes down a funnel and there's only sort of, you know, it constrains your choices
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: This Is Just A Tribute

claims.claim_text: Programmable logic silicon is designed by defining a tile and then replicating it in two dimensions to whatever size the product requires, so the difficult work is the tile and the chips that follow are a multiplication of it.
claims.quote_verbatim: you just multiply the tiles by however big you want the chip to be
claims.speaker: Philip Frieden
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Philip Freidin - Xenodochial Xilinx Ex-Employee

claims.claim_text: Devices manufactured decades ago remain functional after long storage: parts pulled from foam after twenty or thirty years work when fitted, which is consistent enough to be treated as the expectation rather than good luck.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have yet to encounter an old chip I've pulled out, you know, from 20, 30 years ago and it hasn't worked
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: Dedicated integrated circuit testers existed as a product category because devices were expensive enough to justify desoldering them from scrap boards, testing them and returning them to stock. Cheap online component supply removed the economics of that practice rather than any technical change.
claims.quote_verbatim: they were a thing because ICs were expensive
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Tronnort Software Rises Again!

claims.claim_text: Integrated circuit security research borrows its equipment from failure analysis laboratories attached to fabrication plants, using the same instruments the manufacturer uses to inspect a die in order to manipulate or read the chip in ways its designers did not anticipate, after opening the package to expose the bare die.
claims.quote_verbatim: using failure analysis equipment
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dmitry Nedospasov

claims.claim_text: Reading state out of a modern chip with a laser pulse and observing whether a bit flips is conceptually the same technique as reading magnetic core memory, with the difference that core reads destroyed the stored value and required it to be written back, whereas the optical technique on a modern device need not be destructive unless the pulse energy is raised to the point of damage.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's the concept of reading back core memory
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dmitry Nedospasov

claims.claim_text: Recovering a circuit from a finished die is done by etching away the top and working downward through the metal layers, redrawing the connectivity as each is removed; the method is straightforward and the labour is substantial.
claims.quote_verbatim: he basically started. Moving down through the metal layers
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Layout, CAD & Raspberry Pi - Kedogenous Kinetic Knowledge

claims.claim_text: A major supplier in the modern industry sells intellectual property rather than devices, which is a distinction that surprises people who assume every named chip company operates fabrication.
claims.quote_verbatim: Arm don't make chips
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Gremlins in the machine

claims.claim_text: The definition of an integrated circuit in the 1970s and early 1980s covered a timer, an operational amplifier and a family of logic gates, and anything beyond those was built from discrete transistors, which is why designs of that period are dominated by discrete devices.
claims.quote_verbatim: the definition of an integrated circuit back then was 555 timers, 741 op amp and 7400 series logic
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: Integrated circuits reached hobbyist practice years after their introduction: a logic family released in 1964 was aimed at military use, the commercial version followed about two years later, and the first project using integrated circuits appeared in the hobby press in 1967, with the devices costing on the order of a pound and a half each.
claims.quote_verbatim: I found the first IC-based project, which was 1967
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: B Plus Boards and D Minus Cities - Uneath Urban Ubication

claims.claim_text: Space-grade component practice inverted over time. In the Apollo era integrated circuits were new and unreliable, so parts were individually screened and hand-picked to obtain the required reliability, and aerospace was most of the market. Consumer volume has since forced reliability so high, because a failure rate of any appreciable size across tens of millions of units a month is financially impossible, that commercial parts can be used where screened ones once were required.
claims.quote_verbatim: integrated circuits and electronics were so new and they were just unreliable
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Brent and Bryce Salmi

claims.claim_text: Circuit design and software engineering are the same activity of building abstractions: a physical phenomenon is distilled into a discrete component, components are assembled into an integrated circuit with a defined interface whose contents the user is not expected to know, and software repeats the process from machine language upward. Security work consists largely of finding the boundary conditions where those abstractions fail, including at the hardware boundary itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: software engineering is all about building abstractions
claims.speaker: Michal Zalewski
claims.episode_title: The Secret Life of Circuits with lcamtuf / Michał Zalewski

claims.claim_text: The most widely used low-speed serial bus is named for the problem it was created to solve, inter-integrated circuit communication, because a television set could not practically be wired with the multi-gang switches that preceded it.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's the inter-IC communication system
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: The Synergy Bus

claims.claim_text: Products more often fail at a connection than at a semiconductor, whether at a connector or at a wire, and connector selection and maintenance receive correspondingly less attention than they warrant because integrated circuits attract the interest.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of products break down, not because an IC breaks down, but because a connection
claims.episode_title: All the Connectors with Davide Andrea

claims.claim_text: Designing for volume shows in the device count: a product engineered to a low price point reduces to two main chips, one integrating the whole sensor function and one doing the processing, with the remaining functions pushed out to the motors they drive.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you look at the board, it's just two chips
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Boeing, PCBs & Startups - Awful Airplane Aeration

claims.claim_text: Process advances arrive as combinations of dimension and voltage rather than dimension alone: moving from a 22 nanometre process to a 16 nanometre fin-based one came with a core supply voltage of around 0.55 volts, which changes the surrounding design as much as the density does.
claims.quote_verbatim: The core voltage is 0.55 volts
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Robots are coming - Ominous Operational Overhaul

claims.claim_text: Prototyping with milled boards is used specifically to characterise unfamiliar devices: a quick board exists to learn how an integrated circuit behaves and to develop a working driver for it, after which a conventional board is ordered, since bare boards are cheap enough that the milling only buys the first iteration.
claims.quote_verbatim: PCB milling is mainly to test out ICs
claims.speaker: Akiba
claims.episode_title: An interview with Akiba from Freaklabs - Dimissory Diagraphical Debt

claims.claim_text: A mask error has no field remedy, since there is no equivalent of a wire modification on a die, which is what separates a silicon mistake from a board mistake in consequence rather than in kind.
claims.quote_verbatim: There ain't no bodge in a chip
claims.episode_title: Bill and Dave's Excellent Equipment

attribution_notes: ep 401, 425, 455, 527, 566, 703 and 708 sit on the unreliable-attribution list; those claims carry speaker: null and are attributed by content.

ep 2, 15, 88, 96, 128, 199, 253, 597 and 601 label the host where the content is the guest's or vice versa in fused dialogue; claims are attributed to the labelled speaker only where the content is consistent with their role.
Chip-of-the-week product commentary and career anecdote were excluded under the knowledge-only rule.
